name: alera
description: A native, performance-first ADE built with Flutter, Rust, and Ghostty. Run Claude Code, Codex, Amp, and other CLI coding agents in parallel. No Electron.

paragraphs: Website · Docs · Download · Blog · Roadmap · Releases

Alera is a desktop workbench for CLI coding agents. Every agent that runs in a terminal, from Claude Code and Codex to Amp, Cursor, and OpenCode, gets a real terminal in its own Git worktree, and Alera keeps track of which one is working, which one is done, and which one is waiting for you.

It is built with Flutter and Rust for macOS, Windows, and Linux, with no Electron and no bundled browser. A Rust runtime owns every terminal, so agents keep running when you close the window, and the Android companion can answer one from anywhere.
features: Bring your own agent. Alera is terminal-first. Every CLI agent runs in a real PTY, the way it was built to run. There is no chat layer of ours in between and no provider lock-in.

Sessions outlive the window. Close the window and Alera keeps running in the tray with your agents. Quit it and it asks before stopping terminals that still have work, so you can leave the runtime open and come back to…

Native, not a web page. Flutter for the interface, Rust for terminals, processes, and Git, and a maintained fork of the xterm2 emulator for parsing and drawing terminal output. No Electron, no embedded Chromium, no Node…
Know what it costs. The status bar shows each provider's remaining quota and a Resource Manager that attributes CPU and memory to every project, workspace, and terminal.
